source.source_summary: Fully original relationship drama about a partner and her mother secretly maintaining a spreadsheet that scores and manages the relationship.

selected.title: Her Mom Accidentally Sent Me My Boyfriend Score
selected.hook: Her mom accidentally sent me the spreadsheet ranking every person she'd ever dated.
selected.voiceover:
Her mom accidentally sent me the spreadsheet ranking every person she'd ever dated.

My girlfriend, Leah, and I had been together two years when her mom texted me, ‘Ignore the red column. Leah hasn’t seen the latest version.’

Attached was a spreadsheet called ‘Future Husband.’

I thought it was a joke until I opened it.

There were eight names. Mine was at the top, scored on salary, family, appearance, career potential, and something called ‘compliance.’

I got a nine for income and a four for ‘easy to influence.’

Then I noticed the notes.

‘Apartment lease keeps him anchored.’
‘Encourage promotion before engagement.’
‘Discourage weekend trips with college friends.’

Those were actual arguments Leah and I had had.

I called her immediately. She went silent when I mentioned the file.

Then she admitted her mom had been keeping the spreadsheet since our third date.

But Leah had been updating it.

Every few months, she'd send new information so they could ‘spot problems objectively.’

I asked whether our relationship was basically a performance review.

She said I was overreacting because I was ranked first.

That somehow made it worse.

I packed a bag and stayed with my brother.

Now Leah says she'll delete it, stop discussing us with her mom, and start couples counseling.

But I can't stop thinking about that ‘compliance’ score.

Would you rebuild trust, or is secretly grading your partner for two years enough to end it?
selected.youtube_description:
A mistaken text from his girlfriend’s mother exposes a private ‘Future Husband’ spreadsheet ranking him on money, appearance, career potential—and one disturbing category he never knew existed. What starts as bizarre family interference becomes a relationship drama about privacy, manipulation, and how much of a couple’s life should ever be shared with a parent. Could you rebuild trust after learning your relationship had been secretly scored for two years?
